growth_story.headline: American Samoa's income per person slid for a decade as canneries closed, then climbed to a 2022 peak on tuna exports and federal money.
growth_story.arc: From 2003 to 2013 income per person in American Samoa fell by 0.8 percent a year on average, from 13,202 to 11,872 constant dollars. From 2007, the UN Secretariat papers report, federal minimum wage rises and tougher competition led to closures at the tuna canneries that drive the economy, and the September 2009 earthquake and tsunami badly damaged the Satala power plant. From 2014 to 2022 growth averaged 1.7 percent a year but swung hard, from 4.3 percent in 2015 to -5.8 percent in 2017, after investment projects wound down and the Samoa Tuna Processors cannery closed, and back to 5.4 percent in 2020. Federal pandemic grants, canned tuna exports and visitor spending supported the economy in 2022, when income per person reached 13,709, its highest level since the series began in 2002. The economy still rests on federal funds and the last remaining cannery, and no official GDP estimate has been made after 2022.

threads.title: Tuna canning carries exports
threads.text: Tuna canning drives the economy, earns its export income and is the largest source of private jobs. Only a single cannery is left, and the UN papers describe the economy's long-term stability as resting on it and on federal funds.

threads.title: Tsunami, projects end, cannery shuts
threads.text: The earthquake, tsunami and flood of September 2009 severely damaged the Satala power plant. Several public and private investment projects ended or neared their end in 2015, and the Samoa Tuna Processors cannery closed in December 2016. Income per person fell 0.5 percent in 2016 and 5.8 percent in 2017.

threads.title: Fewer people, poorer households
threads.text: The territory's economic development strategy, as the UN reports it, names a shrinking population, very high poverty and a fragile economy. Local workers leave for the United States, and foreign cannery and fishing workers take their place, most cannery workers coming from neighbouring Samoa.

since_last_year.text: In March 2026 the UN Secretariat reported that no official estimate of GDP has been made since 2022, because the US Interior Department's Office of Insular Affairs paused its funding of the work so the territory's source data could be assessed. The data here therefore stop in 2022 and show nothing yet for 2023 onward.

citations.title: American Samoa: Working paper prepared by the Secretariat (A/AC.109/2026/1)
citations.quote: There has been no formal analysis of GDP for American Samoa since 2022.

growth_story.tension: The sources describe a shrinking population and a fragile economy, yet income per person reached its highest level in 2022. The sources' own figures for total output in 2015, 2020 and 2022 show slower growth than the data show for income per person in those years, which fits a falling population: part of the gain in income per person comes from fewer people, not more output.
